questions.question: Explain the difference between a population and a sample using a school survey as the example.
questions.expected_answer: The population is every member of the group the question is about, such as all nine hundred learners at the school. The sample is the part actually asked, such as ninety learners chosen from the register. Results from the sample are used to estimate the population.

questions.question: Why is a sample taken from the tuck shop queue biased for a question about the whole school?
questions.expected_answer: The queue contains only learners who already buy from the tuck shop, so those who bring lunch or have no money are left out. Entry to the sample is connected to the answer, so the sample leans towards current buyers.

questions.question: When should secondary data be chosen over primary data?
questions.expected_answer: When a reliable body such as Statistics South Africa or the municipality already holds data that matches the question and covers a larger population or longer period than you could collect yourself. Record the source and check that its categories fit the question.
